The Alpine vegetation in the western Himalayas is found only up to a height of 3000 metres, while in the eastern Himalayas it is found up to a height of 4000 metres. The reason for this variation in the same mountain range is that
o: eastern Himalayas are higher than western Himalayas

eastern Himalayan rocks are more fertile than the western Himalayan rocks
x: The height of alpine vegetation (tree line) is mainly controlled by local climate—especially temperature, influenced by latitude and maritime effects. The Eastern Himalaya, being nearer the equator and strongly influenced by moisture from the Bay of Bengal, experiences warmer, more humid conditions, allowing the tree line to extend to higher altitudes. In contrast, the Western Himalaya is relatively colder and drier, so alpine conditions occur at lower elevations.

s:
Consider the following statements with reference to- Mediterranean climate:
1. It receives rainfall in winter season.
2. Due to winter solstice, air pressure belts shift to the South.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The Mediterranean climate generally develops between 300 and 400 Latitudes in both hemispheres, primarily on the western sides of continents. A key characteristic of the Mediterranean climate is that rainfall occurs in winter, while summers are usually dry. The development of the Mediterranean climate occurs due to the shifting of pressure and wind belts caused by the northward and southward movement of the sun (Uttarayan and Dakshinayan) During winter (in the Northern Hemisphere), at the time of the winter solstice when sun is over the Tropic of Capricon, the westerly winds originating over the ocean expand into these northern latitudes. Since these mositure wind are associated with temperate cyclones, they cause rainfall. During winter (in the contexst of the Southern Hemisphere), at the time of the summer solstice when the sun is over the tropic of cancer, the expansion of westerly winds originating over the oceans into these latitude bring winter rainfall. Note : Statement (2) is technically incorrect. It is only valid for the mediterranean climate in the Northern Hemisphere. The development of the mediterranean climate is not solely due to the southward shift of pressure belts during the winter solstice but also due to the northward shift to Pressure belts during the summer solstice (which corresponds to winter in the southern Hemisphere).

s: "Each day is more or less the same, the morning is clear and bright with a sea breeze; as the Sun climbs high in the sky, heat mounts up, dark clouds form, then rain comes with thunder and lightning. But the rain is soon over." Which of the following regions is described in the above passage?
x: Option (b) is correct: The passage describes the typical climatic conditions of the equatorial region. • Temperature: Temperature is uniform throughout the year.  The mean monthly temperatures are always around 27° C with very little variation.  There is no winter. [Typical to Equatorial Rainforest Climate]  Cloudiness and heavy precipitation moderate the daily temperature.  Regular land and sea breezes assist in maintaining a truly equable climate.  The diurnal range of temperature is small, and so is the annual range. • Precipitation: Precipitation is heavy and well distributed throughout the year.  Annual average is always above 150 cm. In some regions, the annual average may be as high as 250 – 300 cm.  There is no month without rain (a distinct dry season is absent). The monthly average is above 6 cm most of the time.  There are two periods of maximum rainfall, April and October. [shortly after the equinox]. Least rainfall occurs in June and December [solstice].  The double rainfall peaks coinciding with the equinoxes are a characteristic feature of equatorial climates not found in any other type of climate.  There is much evaporation, and convectional air currents are set up, followed by heavy thunderstorms in the afternoons.

Consider the following description

2. Precipitation occurs throughout the year.
3. Precipitation varies between 50 cm and 250 cm. What is this type of climate?
x: The Marine West Coast Climate occurs on the western margins of continents, poleward of the Mediterranean climatic region. It is found in northwestern Europe, the west coast of North America north of California, southern Chile, southeastern Australia, and New Zealand. Strong maritime influence keeps temperatures moderate throughout the year, making winters milder than those of other regions at similar latitudes. Average summer temperatures range between 15°C and 20°C, while winter temperatures generally range from 4°C to 10°C. Both annual and daily temperature variations are relatively small. Rainfall is received throughout the year, with annual precipitation ranging from 50 cm to 250 cm, depending on local geographical conditions.

o: Creating the artificial rains in some regions
Reducing the frequency and intensity of tropical cyclones
Reducing the adverse effects of solar wind on the Earth
x: The cirrus cloud thinning technique and the injection of sulphate aerosol into the stratosphere are proposed methods aimed at reducing global warming. Cirrus clouds are thin, wispy clouds that form at high altitudes and do not reflect much solar radiation back into space, thereby creating a greenhouse effect. The higher the altitude at which they form, the larger the warming effect on the climate. And in a warmer climate, cirrus clouds form at higher altitudes. These clouds could be thinned out—reducing their warming effect—by seeding them with aerosol particles such as sulfuric or nitric acid, which act as "ice nucleating particles" (INPs).

o: Creating the artificial rains in some regions
Reducing the frequency and intensity of tropical
Reducing the adverse effects of Solar Wind on the
x: Scientists are researching climate engineering to reduce global warming. A major technique related this is the cirrus cloud rarefaction technique. Cirrus clouds are icy crystals of water vapor, which prevent heat reflected from the ground from escaping into outer space. By spraying bismuth triiodide or silver iodide on these clouds they, become sparse. As a result of their rarefaction, their heat absorption capacity is reduced, due to which the terrestrial radiation will go comparatively more into space and thus global warming will be reduced. Similarly, under another proposed geoengineering technique, spraying of sulfate aerosols in the stratosphere would create a layer, that reflects some amount of solar radiation before it reaches the Earth's troposphere, thereby reducing radiation on Earth and thus reducing global warming.
